title: Willow: Ancient Willows You Can Visit
meta_description: Willows nobody has named to species. One in Oslo lies flat on a riverbank and keeps growing; a Manhattan garden class has met under another since 2011.
intro: No source has confirmed the species of these willows, so they carry only the genus, Salix, and each is worth the walk for something other than age. On the bank of the Akerselva in Oslo, a willow that looks to have fallen years ago lies flat on the gravel, and its branches have risen from its back as a row of new stems. On the Rideau Canal in Ottawa, a short, enormously thick trunk covered in burrs carries a crown far wider than it is tall; the reader who sent it knows it as a crack willow. In Manhattan, El Jardin del Paraiso on East 5th Street has a willow a little over three metres round, which NYC Parks added to its Great Trees in 2024 and under which a New School class has met since 2011. Nobody has dated any of the three. If you know one's story, tell us on its page.
